title: A STRANGER IN A FOREIGN LAND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses agreed to stay with the man, who gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage. Zipporah gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, "I have become a foreigner in a foreign land."" - Exodus 2:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives Moses a home, a wife, and a son. Yet the name he chooses for that son tells us what was still in his heart: Gershom — a foreigner in a foreign land.

He had been a Hebrew in an Egyptian palace, and now he was an Egyptian in a Midianite tent. He belonged nowhere. Even with a family and a settled life, something in him remained unsettled.

Many believers know this feeling — in a new city, a new country, a workplace where your faith makes you odd, a family where you are the only one who follows Christ. The ache of not quite belonging is real.

Scripture does not dismiss that ache. It reframes it. Peter calls believers foreigners and exiles in this world (1 Pet 2:11), and Hebrews says the faithful admitted they were strangers here because they were looking for a better country (Heb 11:13-16).

If you feel like you do not fully belong here, that is not a malfunction of your faith. It is a symptom of it. You were made for home, and home is with Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I feel most like an outsider, and have I brought that to God?
2. Am I trying to feel completely at home in a world that is not my final home?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I feel like a stranger, remind me that my true citizenship is with You. Settle my heart in Your promise of home. Amen.
